methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Exact gate-count versus bidirectional positive-growth frontier for the fully restored six-register zero-frame J3 bit block.
scope_change_reason: PR1194/1311 cover the semantic-D substitution and PR1306 covers minimum XOR count. This tests the distinct positive-envelope objective and componentwise boundary cost, not another H2/K repair or a repeat minimum-gate claim.
bottleneck_link: Side result for bit-supplier precision engineering: one additional local XOR lowers the optimal shortest-circuit positive peak from five to the support floor four. Scalar cost rises, the selected complex supplier binds, and no paid recursive profile improvement or supplier admission follows.
stop_rule: Complete all words through seven XORs using a fixed meet-in-the-middle split; check one eight-XOR witness and the universal positive support lower bound. Stop after this one block; no broader search.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json: 216 shortest words; peaks (5,5):108, (6,6):72, (8,8):36; frontier (7,5),(8,4); two complete implementations, semantic controls and certificate mutation rejection.
